messages:
evan-support: Heads-up — ACME reported a spike of 429s right after we pushed the granular throttle change at 08:12 UTC. They say it started ~2m after rollout and affected burst-y endpoints. logs attached: `x-rate-limit: 1000`, `x-client-burst: 120`
ana-sre: on it. Do we have canary metrics for burst windows? want to check per-client token bucket drops vs global gating.
mike-pm: timeline: staged rollout 08:10 -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% at 08:11; we paused at 08:14 when ops-bot alerted. Customer hit 429s at 08:14-08:18.
sasha-platform: quick note: the new policy tightened per-key burst from 200 -> 120 for the high-throughput tier; global threshold unchanged. This was the config variant we promoted.
lee-oncall: ran a quick grep on edge logs. sample: `2026-06-04T08:14:35Z GET /v1/generate 429 client_id=acme-prod token_used=205/120`. That token_used value is the burst counter.
tara-support: ACME reports some internal retries, so they saw a retry storm after 429s, which amplified their error rates — they want rollback or immediate adjustment.
ana-sre: Can we patch a temporary increase for the canary cohort (10% IDs) while we triage? I can flip a per-tag override.
mike-pm: +1 to temporary increase. Product priority: minimize customer pain, keep rollout safeguards. If override fixes it we'll re-evaluate the target burst.
sasha-platform: ops-bot, can you scope which clusters and which traffic slices got the 120-burst policy? need exact rollout map.
ops-bot: rollout-event: policy id `policy:burst-v2-granular` promoted. cohorts: canary-10% (tag: canary-2026-06-04), stage-50% (tag: stage-2026-06-04), global-100% pending. Clusters: use-region-1, use-region-2.
lee-oncall: also seeing elevated 5xx downstream from customer retry storms. Suggest set short-term 2s retry-backoff guidance to customer while we fix.
evan-support: ACME asked for rollback to previous burst=200 immediately. They have SLA impact. Do we have rollback playbook?
sasha-platform: rollback is `policy rollback <id> --target canary-10%` in the control plane. I can execute but want SRE approval for production-wide rollbacks.
ana-sre: I'll do a scoped override first: increase canary burst to 200 for `canary-2026-06-04` then watch 5m window. If errors drop, escalate to a full rollback. Pushing now.
ana-sre: override applied: `policy:burst-v2-granular@canary-2026-06-04` burst=200 -> audit id `audit-7761`. Monitoring: dashboards updated.
mike-pm: thanks. notify ACME that we're applying a temporary fix and we'll follow-up with root cause. keep them in the loop.
tara-support: I told ACME we're applying a temporary lift and will confirm in 5-10m. They appreciate the quick action.
lee-oncall: observing error reduction signal at 08:22 in canary cluster. 429s down ~85% for acme tokens. Downstream 5xx also dropping.
sasha-platform: next steps: 1) gather token usage histograms during burst windows, 2) review retry/backoff patterns client-side, 3) re-run rollout with slower ramp + automated fallback.
evan-support: filing an incident summary for ACME and will attach these notes. Anyone want to add anything before I close this thread?
mike-pm: add a product action: consider defaulting high-throughput customers to a higher soft-burst or an adaptive burst based on observed sustained qps.
nana-sre: add SRE action: improve canary detection rule to pause on per-customer 429 spike (>5%) within 1m window.
sasha-platform: scheduling a post-mortem with oncall and product for tomorrow 14:00 UTC.
evan-support: thanks all. I'll update ACME and mark this resolved once the follow-up PM + SRE actions are captured. :thumbsup:
